review_notes: Selected Table 7 as the principal regression family for the paper’s central claim that growth-fundamental information separates low-BM winners from losers. The paper introduces GSCORE to test future return performance; Table 7 is the full annual regression test of SRET1 with GSCORE and all listed risk/anomaly controls. Table 7 column (2) is retained; column (1) is the reduced controls-only comparison and is not an indispensable construction fit.

GSCORE is a deterministic sum of eight binary signals, so no fitted construction regression is required. The principal portfolio sorting evidence in Table 4 is not itself a regression and is not encoded as a model.

Unresolved source conflict: Section 4.4 prose calls the control LBM and defines it as log(BM), while the Table 7 column is headed BM and its note defines BM as the ratio at formation. The variable is recorded once under the table’s BM label, with the conflict preserved.
The underlying estimator is not reported. The paper reports separate annual regression fits but does not identify OLS or another estimator; method remains null.

dependent_variable.name: SRET1
dependent_variable.definition: One-year size-adjusted return after portfolio formation: the buy-and-hold return for the 12-month period starting May 1 of the year after portfolio formation, less the return in the same period for the firm’s CRSP capitalization decile. Delisting returns are used as described by Shumway (1997).
dependent_variable.formula: 12-month buy-and-hold return beginning May 1 after portfolio formation minus same-period return for the same CRSP capitalization decile; delisting-return adjustment as described in the paper.

evidence.quote: Firm level returns are computed as the buy-and-hold returns for the 12-month and 24-month period starting on the 1st of May of the year after portfolio formation
The returns are size-adjusted by subtracting the returns in the same period for the same capitalization decile as the firm on CRSP.

SRET1 and SRET12 are the size-adjusted buy-and-hold returns respectively, for 1-year and 2-year periods starting May 1st for the year after portfolio formation. When a firm delists, delisting returns are used as in Shumway (1997).

independent_variables.name: GSCORE
independent_variables.definition: Additive index equal to the sum of the eight binary growth-fundamental signals G1–G8. Each signal defaults to 0 and equals 1 when its stated criterion is met: G1, ROA above the contemporaneous median for low-BM firms in the same two-digit SIC industry; G2, cash-flow ROA above that median; G3, cash-flow ROA above ROA; G4, quarterly ROA variance over the prior four years below that median; G5, variance of quarterly year-over-year sales growth, comparing Q0 with Q−4, over the prior four years below that median; G6–G8, respectively, R&D, capital-expenditure and advertising intensity above their corresponding medians. The intensity measures use beginning assets as denominator. G4 and G5 use quarterly data and require at least six quarters; when the required quarterly data are missing, the signals are coded zero rather than dropping the observation. Industry medians are at the two-digit SIC level within low-BM firms.

evidence.quote: GSCORE is the sum of eight fundamental signals, G1:G8, tailored for growth firms. G1:G8 have a default value of 0 and equal 1 if the following criteria are met respectively.
I define the first growth signal, G1, to equal 1 if a firm’s ROA is greater than the contemporaneous median ROA for all low BM firms in the same industry and 0 otherwise.
ROA, defined as the ratio of net income before extraordinary items scaled by average total assets.
I define the second growth signal, G2, to equal 1 if a firm’s cash flow ROA exceeds the contemporaneous median for all low BM firms in the same industry and 0 otherwise.
G3 is defined to equal if a firm’s cash flow from operations exceeds net income and 0 otherwise.
G4 is defined to equal 1 if a firm’s earnings variability is less than the contemporaneous median for all low BM firms in the same industry and 0 otherwise.
G5 is defined to equal 1 it a firm’s sale growth variability is less than the contemporaneous median for all low BM firms in the same industry and 0 otherwise.

G6, G7 and G8 are defined to equal 1 if a firm’s R&D, capital expenditure and advertising intensity respectively, are greater than the contemporaneous medians of the corresponding variables for all low BM firms in the same industry and 0 otherwise. The intensity of R&D, capital expenditure and advertising are measured by deflating these variables by beginning assets.

The two signals related to naı ̈ve extrapolation, i.e. earnings variability and sales growth variability (G4,G5) are generated from quarterly financials of the past 4 years, with the constraint that at least six quarters information be available.
If these data are missing, the observations are not deleted, but the signals are coded as zeroes.
Industry medians are calculated at the two-digit SIC level within low BM firms.
I measure growth variability as the variance of a firm’s year over year sales growth (Q0 compared to Q)4) over the past 4 years using quarterly information.

sample_extraction.data_section_full_text:
3.1. Sample Selection


I start with all firms in COMPUSTAT between 1978 and 2001. Using appropriate
quarterly financial information, I create year-to-date annual financials for firms as of
or closest to the end of December. All firms in the sample hence have financial
information for the period ending at the end of December, November or October. <sup>6</sup> If
adequate quarterly information is not available, the information from the latest fiscal
year prior to December is used. This ensures that there is no look-ahead bias in the
computation of the signals, even if it means that the data may sometimes be dated.

Firms with negative BM ratios are deleted. The distribution from the prior year is
used to calculate the cutoffs for groups of firms based on the BM. The primary focus
of this paper is on the firms in the lowest quintile of BM ratios (growth firms). In
later tests, I also analyze firms in the highest quintile of BM (value firms).

Since the calculation of many of the signals used in the GSCORE metric
requires comparison with industry medians, I require that a firm have at least
three other firms in the same industry (defined by two-digit SIC code) in the same
